q: My mom has said before she doesn’t want to be a grandma till she’s 60.
cx: 19, six weeks, living in her mother's house; hasn't told her yet.

q: I don’t feel like the happy, glowing pregnant woman everyone talks about. I feel exhausted, sick, overwhelmed
cx: 10+3, nauseous every day, crying for weeks; wasn't sure she could have another child.

q: I’m wondering if I tell my boss but point out I would prefer it to stay between us since I’m early in (is that a hippa thing?) and seeing if she is fine with me working from home until I get past this stage?
cx: First trimester with her second child; hybrid job, three office days a week.

q: I don’t want to lose my job over “morning” sickness (it’s never just in the morning 🙄) should I rope HR into it?
cx: Kind boss, difficult department director she hopes to keep out of it.

q: I played outside with my daughter today for a few hours and by the end I was ready for a nap.
cx: Says this pregnancy is 'the polar opposite' of her first.

q: At the end they turned to my husband who was there and said “it just means you have to wait longer to resume sex. I know that sucks doesn’t it?”
cx: First-time mother at her six-week check, told she needs a repair; felt her concerns were disregarded.

q: My in-laws constantly ask about my due date even though I've told them multiple times. My FIL keeps asking whether the doctor said exactly when the baby will come.
cx: First-time mother, almost 37 weeks, a doctor studying for exams.

q: Sometimes I feel like my baby has become everyone's project.
cx: Her mother is also eager; she feels nobody thinks about her any more.

q: I keep having this irrational fear that once my baby is born, everyone will want to take the baby from me, pass the baby around, and I'll have no control.
cx: Asks how others set boundaries without family drama.

q: husband and I didn't tell anyone that I'm going into labor. It was just my husband and me , and it's the best decision we ever took!
cx: Update two months later, after the birth.

q: My parents still call and try to assert dominance by telling me how to parent my kid , i strictly put boundaries and told them to stay in their limits . And I limited calls to oncr a week .
cx: How she handles her own parents after the birth.

q: My company changed my manager, and ever since then my stress has gone through the roof. I constantly feel overwhelmed, like I have 300 things to do at once, and pregnancy brain has made everything so much harder.
cx: 17 weeks; works because she enjoys it, not for money; asks if anyone quit while pregnant.

q: It’s been between 90-105 the last 2 weeks but even in 80 degree temps I can’t be outside for very long. I’m even sweating in the AC.
cx: Almost 25 weeks in southern Virginia, living on a working homestead.

q: It feels like I’m going to be on house arrest once I reach third trimester. I will NEVER be pregnant in the summer again 🫠
cx: Says she used to enjoy the sweat; now it doesn't feel responsible.

q: It’s too early to tell anyone at work that I’m pregnant so can’t use it as an excuse to underperform (I don’t think anyone has been pregnant in the history of this company tbh).
cx: 34, 7-8 weeks, AI startup with a '996' culture; often works 7AM-10PM and commutes two trains.

q: my mom keeps reminding me that we grew up and she gave birth while we lived in poverty. And that it’s possible. My ob reminded me that women have been doing this for thousands of years and even she was in residency while pregnant.
cx: What her mother and OB say when she describes her workload; it adds to her guilt.

q: I feel guilty for bringing a child into the world when I’m going to have zero time to raise him/her after mat leave and going back to work.
cx: Can't quit for fear of not getting back into the tech job market.

q: All of these stories made me feel SO much less alone.
cx: After other working mothers shared their own stories in reply.

q: To say I am overwhelmed with the info dumping on the internet is putting it lightly. I feel like I should have been doing more research years in the past with the amount of stuff!
cx: 24 weeks with her first, posting in a new-parents forum.

q: Between the baby needs, the birthing info, and the postpartum stuff I am exhausted. How do I manage all this information and know what is right or wrong?
cx: Asks strangers how to sort what she is reading.

q: I keep getting overwhelmed by the random medical information (today I learned about some sort of probe the might want to put into my baby’s skull to hear the heartbeat better?).
cx: What happened when she started researching the birth itself.

q: Doesnt help we’re caring for an almost 3 year old and 7 week old, and the newborn still refuses to sleep longer than 2 hours at a time so we’re exhausted.
cx: Seven weeks after her second son; recovery faster than the first time.

q: It feels like I have no idea what I’m doing despite having twins before this pregnancy.
cx: 36+5, after an earlier high-risk pregnancy; repeated monitoring visits leave her unsettled.

q: So swollen, so worried about everything, and OB appointments feel so unsuccessful at making it any more comfortable.
cx: The last month countdown, due in 22 days.

q: AND all of our family lives in other states and it’s really stressful trying to figure out getting someone here to help with our toddler while I’m in labor.
cx: 34+ weeks with her second; part of why a scheduled date appeals to her.

q: my midwife LITERALLY told me to stop eating everything except protein, and that I should just eat eggs for the rest of my pregnancy, to stop the baby from growing anymore.
cx: After a scan showed a large baby; she has distrusted the clinic since.

q: I finally got financially caught up and want to be able to get things for our nursery, save, or sometimes spend a little money on me like a pregnancy pillow to help me sleep, prenatal massage
cx: 34 weeks, server and student, paying the rent for two months since her boyfriend lost his job.

q: I’ve been looking at those BabyCenter articles every week about each week of pregnancy, and they always show a picture of your innards with the baby inside to show how big they are.
cx: 15 weeks; skipped ahead in the weekly articles.

q: the 35+ week ones are TERRIFYING THE BABY IS SO BIG!!! I’m like how THE FUCK Is that gonna come out of me lol!
cx: What the late-pregnancy weekly illustrations did to her.

q: My back is killing me from all the yoga ball sessions. And don't even think of sitting down for a rest, she knows the moment you do and will make sure of it.
cx: A father of a hard-to-settle 2-month-old, first child.

q: I feel guilty towards my two for having another baby when life is so full with all of us here already.
cx: 37, six weeks, children 12 and 9 from a previous marriage plus a 17-year-old stepdaughter.

q: now I feel like I’ll have less time with this baby and I’ll still be “mummying” in my 50s.
cx: Had her first two at 25 and 28.
